legalizer.finding: Read/write boundaries are independent only with decouple_rw1. With decouple_rw0 both lengths use min(source page,maxburst boundary,destination page,maxburst boundary), and their machines advance together.

frontend.finding: decouple_rw comes from conf.decouple; default max256 requires conf.deburst0. decouple_aw is forced0 but ignored if RAWCouplingAvail0.

actual_instantiation.finding: Production RAW_COUPLING_AVAIL0. Old stage54 multi_actual_dma_top.sv380/439 also0. Do not describe an enabled first-R coupler as current production hardware.

AW_credit_additional_condition: If a candidate enables RAWCouplingAvail1 while decouple_aw0, one source burst firstR provides only one AW release credit in idma_channel_coupler.sv105/142-159. Two original destinationAW from one sourceAR need an explicit legal length/envelope release design or a deliberately bypassed coupler with equivalent admission; job binding fields alone do not prove second AW reachability. This is source inspection, not an executed hardware bug.

geometry.flags: decouple_rw1 AND deburst0; RAWCouplingAvail0 for unchanged current release interface
geometry.one_source: Source page offset0 or0x800, N256 -> one256-wordsourceAR. Dest0x818 independently gives253+3; dest0x810254+2; dest0x820252+4.
geometry.coupled_control: With decouple_rw0 the first source is cut to253,254 or252 respectively together with firstdestination; originalsourceAR256 is not produced. This configuration is a concrete ordinary source-split control, not the proposed unsplit case.

contribution_scope: The single-flow capacity proof explains a safe storage boundary; do not infer new published capability merely because our own old sponsor prototype blocks it. A ordinary DMA allowed to read before the next destination permission and with enough reserved tail storage may already reach it. The multi-consumer all-partial unsplit-read frontier, actual shared return dependencies, total metadata and complete-cost benefit are the remaining specific contribution questions.
